items.title: AI Companies Still Haven’t Delivered on Their Biggest Promises
items.summary: Dario Amodei almost never posts — but when a prominent investor claimed on All In that Anthropic's CEO believes his company might one day be the only private company left, Dario waded into X with a two-post defense of his views on regulation, messaging, and trust. His most quotable concession doubles as the episode's title: the most accurate criticism of AI companies is that they haven't yet delivered on their big promises. Plus: ZAI's GLM 5.3 squeezes near-frontier performance out of a mid-sized model, Anthropic keeps its best model for itself, and investors float a $2 trillion IPO.
items.whyItMatters: Policy and risk stories often become product constraints later, especially around data access, safety claims, export rules, and copyright.

brief.whatHappened: AI Companies Still Haven’t Delivered on Their Biggest Promises
brief.whoItAffects: Product builders, platform users, and anyone depending on model access or data rights.
brief.practicalImpact: Policy moves can become tomorrow's product limits, compliance burden, or availability issue.

items.title: Pennsylvania just made itself one of the hardest US states to build a data centre in
items.summary:
Governor Josh Shapiro signed an executive order on Tuesday that makes Pennsylvania one of the harder places in America to build an AI data centre. The order strips data centres from the state’s permit fast-track programme, blocks environmental review until developers have secured local approval, and bars state agencies from signing non-disclosure agreements on data centre projects. items.title: SK Hynix will buy back $28.6bn of its own shares, the biggest repurchase in Korean corporate history
items.summary:
SK Hynix will buy back 40 trillion won of its own stock, about $28.6bn at prevailing exchange rates, in what Korean media are calling the largest repurchase ever announced by a listed company in the country. items.summary:
